{{Short description|Two special graphs in graph theory}}
[[File:Triple torus illustration.png|thumb|150px|[[Triple torus|Surface of genus 3]]]]
In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''Klein graphs''' are two different but related [[regular graph]]s, each with 84 edges. Each can be embedded in the orientable [[Surface (topology)|surface]] of [[Surface (topology)#Classification_of_closed_surfaces|genus]] 3, in which they form [[dual graph]]s.

==The cubic Klein graph==
{{infobox graph
 | name = 3-regular Klein graph
 | image = [[Image:Klein_graph.svg|250px]]
 | namesake = Felix Klein
 | vertices = 56
 | edges = 84
 | automorphisms= 336
 | girth = 7
 | radius = 6
 | diameter = 6
 | chromatic_number = 3 
 | chromatic_index = 3
 | properties = [[Symmetric graph|Symmetric]]<br>[[Cubic graph|Cubic]]<br>[[Hamiltonian graph| Hamiltonian]]
|book thickness=3|queue number=2}}

This is a 3-[[regular graph|regular]] ([[Cubic graph|cubic]]) graph with 56 vertices and 84 edges, named after [[Felix Klein]].

It is [[Hamiltonian graph|Hamiltonian]], has [[chromatic number]] 3, [[chromatic index]] 3, radius 6, diameter 6 and [[girth (graph theory)|girth]] 7. It is also a 3-[[k-vertex-connected graph|vertex-connected]] and a 3-[[k-edge-connected graph|edge-connected]] graph. It has [[book thickness]] 3 and [[queue number]] 2.<ref>Wolz, Jessica; ''Engineering Linear Layouts with SAT.'' Master Thesis, University of Tübingen, 2018</ref>

It can be embedded in the [[Manifold#Genus_and_the_Euler_characteristic|genus]]-3 orientable [[Manifold|surface]] (which can be represented as the [[Klein quartic]]), where it forms the Klein map with 24 heptagonal faces, [[Schläfli symbol]] {7,3}<sub>8</sub>.

According to the ''Foster census'', the Klein graph, referenced as F056B, is the only cubic symmetric graph on 56 vertices which is not [[Bipartite graph|bipartite]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Conder | first1 = M. | author1-link = Marston Conder
 | last2 = Dobcsányi | first2 = P.
 | journal = J. Combin. Math. Combin. Comput.
 | pages = 41–63
 | title = Trivalent symmetric graphs up to 768 vertices
 | volume = 40
 | year = 2002}}.</ref>

It can be derived from the 28-vertex [[Coxeter graph]].<ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Dejter | first = Italo J.
 | arxiv = 1002.1960
 | doi = 10.1002/jgt.20597
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Journal of Graph Theory
 | mr = 2916063
 | pages = 1–9
 | title = From the Coxeter graph to the Klein graph
 | volume = 70
 | year = 2012}}</ref> 

===Algebraic properties===
The automorphism group of the Klein graph is the group PGL<sub>2</sub>(7) of order 336, which has
[[(2,3,7) triangle group|PSL<sub>2</sub>(7)]] as a normal subgroup. This group acts transitively on its half-edges, so the Klein graph is a [[symmetric graph]]. 

The [[characteristic polynomial]] of this 56-vertex Klein graph is equal to <math> 
x^7 \,(x-3)\,(x+2)^6 \left(x^2-2\right)^6 \left(x^2+x-4\right)^7 \left(x^2-2 x-1\right)^8 </math>

== The 7-regular Klein graph {{anchor|The 7-valent Klein graph}}==

{{infobox graph
 | name = 7-regular Klein graph
 | image = [[Image:Klein-graph-7-valent_Hamiltonian.svg|250px]]
 | namesake = Felix Klein
 | vertices = 24
 | edges = 84
 | automorphisms= 336
 | girth = 3
 | radius = 3
 | diameter = 3
 | chromatic_number = 4 
 | chromatic_index = 7 
 | properties = [[Symmetric graph|Symmetric]]<br>[[Hamiltonian graph| Hamiltonian]]
}}

This is a 7-[[regular graph|regular]] graph with 24 vertices and 84 edges, named after [[Felix Klein]].

It is [[Hamiltonian graph|Hamiltonian]], has [[chromatic number]] 4, [[chromatic index]] 7, radius 3, diameter 3 and [[girth (graph theory)|girth]] 3. <!--It is also a 3-[[k-vertex-connected graph|vertex-connected]] and a 3-[[k-edge-connected graph|edge-connected]] graph.-->

It can be embedded in the genus-3 orientable surface, where it forms the dual of the Klein map, with 56 triangular faces, [[Schläfli symbol]] {3,7}<sub>8</sub>.<ref>{{cite journal
  |last1=Schulte
  |first1=Egon
  |last2=Wills
  |first2=J. M.
  |title=A Polyhedral Realization of Felix Klein's Map {3, 7}<sub>8</sub> on a Riemann Surface of Genus 3
  |journal=J. London Math. Soc.
  |year=1985
  |volume=s2-32
  |issue=3
  |pages=539–547
 |url=http://jlms.oxfordjournals.org/content/s2-32/3/539.abstract|doi=10.1112/jlms/s2-32.3.539
 }}</ref>

It is the unique [[distance-regular graph]] with intersection array <math>\{7,4,1; 1,2,7\}</math>; however, it is not a [[distance-transitive graph]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Brouwer|first1=Andries|author-link1=Andries Brouwer|last2=Cohen|first2=Arjeh|last3=Neumaier|first3=Arnold|title=Distance-Regular Graphs|url=https://archive.org/details/distanceregularg00brou|url-access=limited|publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]]|year=1989|isbn=978-0-387-50619-7|page=[https://archive.org/details/distanceregularg00brou/page/n398 386]}}</ref>

===Algebraic properties===
The automorphism group of the 7-valent Klein graph is the same group of order 336 as for the cubic Klein map, likewise acting transitively on its half-edges.

The [[characteristic polynomial]] of this 24-vertices Klein graph is equal to <math>(x-7) (x+1)^7 (x^2-7)^8</math>.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=van Dam|first1=E. R.|last2=Haemers|first2=W. H.|last3=Koolen|first3=J. H.|last4=Spence|first4=E.|title=Characterizing distance-regularity of graphs by the spectrum|journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory|J. Combin. Theory Ser. A]]|year=2006|volume=113|issue=8|pages=1805–1820|doi=10.1016/j.jcta.2006.03.008|doi-access=free}}</ref>
